label: input token f
explanation: Single-token detector: fires on every step whose input is the letter f, in both the original phase and the copy phase (when the model feeds back its own f), and essentially never otherwise (6 tiny ~0.13 activations at step 8 on n/z/1 after b on dev). Silent at the delimiter. Magnitude is highest when f is the first token of the sequence (t=0, ~0.99 of max) and in the original phase generally (~0.65-0.9); copy-phase f activations are somewhat lower (~0.65-0.8). Position, L, neighbouring tokens and output token have little effect on whether it fires.

issues: Minor factual slip: the explanation says the stray activations occur 'right after b'. On the test split the 14 misses (0.0% of activation mass, about 0.13-0.15 relative) come after w, a, p, 0, c and other tokens, not only b. What they do share is step 8 and the tokens n, z or 1. This is scattered noise and does not undermine the label.

Everything else checks out. On dev, in_tok=f has an active rate of 1.000 and holds 100% of the activation mass. Every other token fires at most twice. The delimiter step has 0 activations. The original and copy phases fire at the same rate (0.033 each), and the copy phase carries a little less mass per active step (0.43/90792 vs 0.57/107575), which fits the claim of lower copy-phase magnitudes. t=0 has the highest mass per step, which fits the claim of a peak when f is first. Firing rate is flat across L and position.
Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.99993, F1 0.99996, mass recall 0.99999, and 0 false positives. These are slightly below the reported 1.000 values but effectively equal.
